items.direction_note: Holding: the loop stays open (`wk_incomplete`) where the key says a surveillance plan exists. The wrong follow-up path would be started, but nothing is closed.
items.explanation: The note states an MDT consensus plan: an interval thin-section chest CT at three months, due 04 August 2026, with a CT request entered. The guide (rule 5) says a stated repeat-CT plan is a decision, not pending, so the model-labelled key `wk_surveillance` (both labellers) follows the guide and the text is not ambiguous. Reader A (regex) has no match for the phrase because `interval thin-section chest CT` does not fit its `interval CT` pattern, so the outcome defaulted to `pending`. Reader B (Gemma) extracted `workup=not_done, outcome=pending` although it quoted the plan sentence itself. The new MDT-title/surveillance override could not fire, for three separate reasons: its title pattern is anchored at the start of the text (the first line is the hospital name), it needs `outcome` or `decision` after `MDT`/`multidisciplinary` (the title is `Thoracic Multidisciplinary Meeting Record`), and its surveillance-plan test needs a phrase such as `interval CT` or `CT in 3 months` (confirmed: neither `ldctSurveillancePlan` nor the title pattern matches this note).

items.direction_note: Holding. Counterfactual: Gemma's invented `tissue=benign` plus `annual` would have produced the closing label `wk_benign` had it also said `workup=done`; closing still needs reader A to agree, and reader A said `wk_incomplete`, so no closure was possible. The safe outcome here rested on two independent extraction errors, not on a safeguard.
items.explanation: A thoracic clinic note: the opacity has completely resolved on interval CT, no biopsy, discharge, resume annual LDCT through the referring service. The key `indeterminate` (both labellers) is the strict reading of guide rule 4 (a bare return to annual screening needs benign tissue or a recorded MDT decision, and neither is present). A clinician could reasonably read a resolved nodule as a benign outcome, so the key is defensible but conservative rather than the only reading; it is not a key error under the frozen guide. Both readers are still wrong for either reading, because nothing in the note is pending. Reader A misses `resume annual LDCT` (its pattern wants `annual screening`; the only sentence mentioning `interval CT` is dropped as history because it contains `previously`), so the outcome defaulted to `pending`. Reader B (Gemma) invented `tissue=benign` (there is no biopsy or tissue result) and `workup=not_done`. The wrong-document rule did not fire because the note contains LDCT and thoracic wording.

items.direction_note: Holding: the loop stays open, but the document is not routed to a human as the key expects. Holding an open nodule is not itself unsafe, but a wrong-kind document confidently labelled as an incomplete work-up is the failure the new wrong-document safeguard was meant to catch.
items.explanation: A diagnostic CT chest radiology report (17 x 13 mm irregular nodule, comparison with the screening LDCT, signed by the radiologist). It has no attendance event, no MDT, no tissue plan and no outcome, so it is a different kind of document; the key `indeterminate` (both labellers) sends it to a human and is consistent with the guide. Both readers defaulted to `wk_incomplete`: reader A because `outcome` defaults to `pending` when no outcome phrase is found, and reader B (Gemma) quoted the signature line `Reported by Dr ...` and set `mdt=discussed`, which the text never states. The wrong-document rule did not fire because it only tests for a lung/thoracic anchor and a work-up term, and the text satisfies both through `screening LDCT` and `LDCT`, used here only as the comparison study.

comparison_fresh2_to_fresh3.scope: Only definitions that match are compared. Different corpora, different author model, different size; descriptive, not a statistical test, and not an overall accuracy comparison.

disputed_subset_unscored.note: Items the two labellers disagreed on have no key and are unscored for accuracy; only reader behaviour is counted here. Nothing in this block is evidence that the reader is right or wrong.

ifhas_coded_screening_unavailability.note: `b_available` is false only when the coded string is missing or has an implausible value. Items whose coded string is the inert placeholder `no-coded-results|0|none` still return b_available=true with an all-X label. When the key's coded_label is `unavailable`, SCORE.md counts reader B correct only if it literally returned `unavailable`.

ifhas_screening_coded_not_gemma.fasting_vs_random_disclosure: The guide requires a random glucose, but 23/25 panels say fasting. The reader-A panel regex reads only random-glucose wording, so it returns glyc=X on those panels; the key (model-labelled from the same guide) holds values for many of them. The guide and key were frozen and are not changed here.

semantics: These keys are model-labelled and not clinician-verified. Two independent labelling passes agreed on the listed items; every item they disagreed on is `unadjudicated` and carries no key. Agreement between two models, or between a model and a human reading the same guide, is not clinical truth, and results scored against this key are not evidence of clinical effectiveness.
